claims.text: The equimolar CoCrFeNiTi solid-solution alloy has inherently high stacking-fault energy.
High stacking-fault energy in this alloy favors planar dislocation slip.
Planar slip in this alloy involves minimal dislocation interaction and accumulation.
Limited dislocation interaction and accumulation produce weak work hardening.
Weak work hardening accounts for the low hardness and yield strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi retains favorable ductility despite its low hardness and yield strength.
The applicable initial material is as-cast, equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple single-phase solid-solution state.
TEM examination of deformed specimens can be used to characterize deformation-induced microstructural evolution.
The controlled comparison is between as-cast specimens and specimens pre-strained by cold working during subsequent in situ tensile or compression loading.
The proposed loading range is room-temperature uniaxial deformation at strain rates of approximately 10^-4 to 10^-3 s^-1.
The relevant structural mediators are dislocation arrangement, dislocation density, stacking faults, and the presence or absence of nanotwinning.
Rapid dislocation glide prevents formation of dense dislocation forests in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
As-cast specimens under in situ loading will exhibit sparse dislocations, planar slip, and little pile-up or tangling.
After cold working, subsequent loading will produce only a marginal increase in dislocation density.
Cold-worked specimens will show no significant forest hardening upon reloading.
Significant dislocation entanglement, pronounced cross-slip, or nanotwinning would falsify the proposed predominant planar-slip mechanism.
Nanotwinning or recovery could concurrently influence dislocation behavior.
